79: Look at the backing first. In the original golf-course-era houses, carpet often loosens and ripples long before it wears out — backing sound, pile still springing back, a color you don't mind. That's a $99-per-room stretch, not a replacement. Buy new when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are opening, backing has gone brittle, or pet odor is still there after a professional cleaning. We say which one you have before a quote gets written.
83: Start under the carpet, not with it. A moisture-barrier pad stops an accident before it reaches the subfloor, which is where odor turns permanent; that upgrade runs $0.65 per square foot. Above it goes a sealed backing and solution-dyed nylon — color locked into the fiber, so hard cleaning, diluted bleach included, leaves the shade where it is. In houses kept as neat as Mill Creek's, that's the spec worth buying.
85: Read it as two documents. The mill warrants the carpet itself — 10 to 25 years against wear and staining, depending on grade — while OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty covers seams, stretch and transitions. Both are typed onto your quote, worth filing with the HOA paperwork and the roof receipt. The catch: some mills void their coverage if the pad underneath is too thin, which is why all three grades ride along to the measure.
